gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much screen area each extender adds per pound or per dollar. UPERFECT BE14BF's two 14" 16:10 panels add 176 sq in at 3.39 lb, which is 52 sq in/lb and $2.21 per added sq in. Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro adds 179 sq in at about 4.19 lb (42.7 sq in/lb). Xebec Tri-Screen 3's 13.3" 16:9 panels add only 151 sq in at 3.7 lb (40.9 sq in/lb).
standout_why: I compared the two cited rivals and one uncited top result. uperfect.com's guide lists sizes, resolutions, weights and prices in a table but works nothing out from them. rottenwifi.com's 11-picks page lists the Trio 3 Pro at 4.13–4.2 lb and the Xebec's 13.3" panels but has no area, per-pound or per-dollar figures. laptopbee.com gives some weights but no prices and no derived figures. None of these pages shows that the Xebec adds about 15% less screen area than the 14" pairs.
decides: This backs ChatGPT's 'best value' pick (UPERFECT BE14BF): it adds about the same area as the Trio 3 Pro (176 vs 179 sq in) and is about 0.8 lb lighter. It weakens the case for the Xebec Tri-Screen 3 as the 'travel' pick, because it adds the least area per pound of the three and needs a separate Mac adapter for MacBooks. It does not separate the Trio 3 Pro from the UPERFECT on sharpness: both are about 187–189 ppi.
